body.en: Far from the surface, mgh no longer works because g changes. Taking the potential energy to be zero at infinity, the potential energy of a mass m at distance r from the centre of the earth is $V(r) = -GM_Em/r$. It is negative because gravity is attractive: work must be done to pull the mass away to infinity. The *gravitational potential* is $V/m = -GM_E/r$.
body.kn: ಮೇಲ್ಮೈಯಿಂದ ದೂರದಲ್ಲಿ g ಬದಲಾಗುವುದರಿಂದ mgh ಅನ್ವಯಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಅನಂತದಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಶೂನ್ಯ ಎಂದು ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಂಡರೆ, r ದೂರದಲ್ಲಿ V = −GMm/r. ಗುರುತ್ವ ಆಕರ್ಷಕವಾದ್ದರಿಂದ ಇದು ಋಣ.

Far from the earth, mgh fails. Taking zero at infinity, the potential energy is minus G M m over r: negative because gravity attracts.
To escape, the kinetic energy at launch must at least cancel the negative potential energy at the surface.
For the earth, the escape speed is about 11.2 kilometres per second, whatever the mass or the direction of launch.

body.en: The *escape speed* is the least speed with which a body must be projected from the surface to reach infinity. Setting $\tfrac12 mv_e^2 = GM_Em/R_E$ gives $v_e = \sqrt{2GM_E/R_E} = \sqrt{2gR_E} \approx 11.2$ km/s for the earth. It does not depend on the mass of the body or the direction of projection. On the Moon it is only about 2.3 km/s, which is why the Moon has no atmosphere.

heading.en: Gravitational Potential Energy, Escape Speed and Satellites

tagline.en: Gravitational potential energy and potential, escape speed, orbital speed and period of Earth satellites, and the energy of an orbiting satellite; geostationary and polar satellites for ISC.

myth.en: Astronauts in the International Space Station float because there is no gravity up there.

truth.en: At the station's height (about 400 km) g is still about 8.7 m/s². Astronauts feel weightless because they and the station are both in free fall around the Earth. We link 'floating' with 'no gravity'. In fact gravity is exactly what keeps the station in orbit; since everything falls with the same acceleration, nothing presses on the floor, so there is no feeling of weight.

say.en: Throw a stone up fast enough and it never comes back. The escape speed is the least launch speed that lets a body just reach infinity (where its KE becomes zero).

A satellite of mass $m$ in a circular orbit of radius $r = R_E + h$ is held by gravity, which supplies the centripetal force: $\dfrac{mv^2}{r} = \dfrac{GM_Em}{r^2}$. This gives the orbital speed and the period.

goal.en: Gravitational potential energy and potential, escape speed, orbital speed and period of Earth satellites, and the energy of an orbiting satellite; geostationary and polar satellites for ISC.

task.en: Match each quantity to its value or formula.

explain.en: For a circular orbit $E = -K$ and $U = 2E$. Escape needs $\sqrt2$ times the low-orbit speed.

takeaway.en: $U = -GMm/r$ (zero at infinity); $V = -GM/r$; mgh is the near-surface form.

In fact gravity is exactly what keeps the station in orbit; since everything falls with the same acceleration, nothing presses on the floor, so there is no feeling of weight.

problem.en: Calculate the escape speed from the earth (g = 9.8 m/s², R_E = 6.4 × 10⁶ m).

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Calculate the escape speed from the earth (g = 9.8 m/s², R_E = 6.4 × 10⁶ m).

say.en: Let us solve this together. Calculate the escape speed from the earth (g equals 9.8 metres per second squared, R E equals 6.4 times 10 to the power 6 metres).
v e equals the square root of 2gR E equals the square root of (2 times 9.8 times 6.4 times 10 to the power 6).
v e equals the square root of (1.2544 times 10 to the power 8) equals 1.12 times 10 to the power 4 metres per second.
So the answer is 11.2 kilometres per second.

homework.en: A planet has 4 times the mass and the same radius as the earth. Find its escape speed (answer: 22.4 km/s).

narration.en: Recap. Gravitational PE: V = −GMm/r, zero at infinity. Escape speed v_e = √(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km/s for the earth. v_e does not depend on the mass of the body or the direction of throw.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಗುರುತ್ವ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ ಶಕ್ತಿ V = −GMm/r, ಅನಂತದಲ್ಲಿ ಶೂನ್ಯ. ಭೂಮಿಗೆ ವಿಮೋಚನಾ ವೇಗ v_e = √(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km/s. v_e ಕಾಯದ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಅಥವಾ ಎಸೆಯುವ ದಿಕ್ಕನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

title.en: Earth satellites and the energy of an orbiting satellite
title.kn: ಭೂಮಿಯ ಉಪಗ್ರಹಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಕಕ್ಷೆಯಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಉಪಗ್ರಹದ ಶಕ್ತಿ

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. Gravitational PE: V equals -GMm/r, zero at infinity.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ಗುರುತ್ವ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ ಶಕ್ತಿ V equals -GMm/r, ಅನಂತದಲ್ಲಿ ಶೂನ್ಯ.

say.en: Escape speed v e equals the square root of 2gR is approximately 11.2 kilometres per second for the earth.
say.kn: ಭೂಮಿಗೆ ವಿಮೋಚನಾ ವೇಗ v e equals the square root of 2gR is approximately 11.2 kilometres per second.

say.en: v e does not depend on the mass of the body or the direction of throw.
say.kn: v e ಕಾಯದ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಅಥವಾ ಎಸೆಯುವ ದಿಕ್ಕನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.
